asr.full_text: Hello, everyone. Welcome back to the show My name is Catherine Gu, Head of Product for Digital Asset at Solano Foundation. Here with me today, I have Josh from Coinbase. joining us. Josh, welcome to the show. How you doing? Thanks. Doing well. Thanks for having me. Yeah, like maybe tell us just a little bit about your role at Coinbase and what is the Coinbase developer platform? Yeah, so I'm a group product manager here at Coinbase. I look after our wallets and a variety of other on-chain tools that we have. Coinbase developer platform, you can think of as the infrastructure arm of Coinbase. So, kind of, doing for Coinbase what AWS did for Amazon, and so we're taking all the infrastructure that Coinbase has built up over the last 15 years and scaled and secured to power its own products. And we're enabling anyone that's building on the blockchain that needs rails for payments, trading, wallets, stablecoins, and so on, to use that same infrastructure to build whatever it is they'd like to build. Fantastic. And of course, as the two developer platforms meet, I suppose, you know, there's a lot of synergies that we're trying to explore here. So maybe, just share a little bit about what is that, and especially as you know, for SDP is very much focused with the institutional lens, right? So what is the user experience do you think is going to look like within SDP, right now, and also down the road? Yeah, so I think the starting point is that we were a day one launch partner for the Solana developer platform for our coin based developer platform, or CBP, server wallet specifically. And so server wallet is a programmatic API based wallet that is developer custodian. So the developer controls the wallet through their API key key, and this other piece of cryptographic material called the wallet secret. The wallet private keys themselves are secured in coinbase infrastructure entrusted enclaves that Coinbase doesn't have access to fully controlled by the developer with really rich policy engines and other security features, highly scalable and used in coinbases own products across millions of customers. So that's what the developer gets out of the box in day 1, conveniently wrapped in SDP so that if they're building on Solana, they can use these server wallets for AI agents and also for their apps for things like backend, payment orchestration, treasury management, whatever it might be. So that's really seamless. That makes things really easy for a Solana developer that needs a wallet that they control, that's programmatic for their backend. That's kind of the first part of your question. It's like the minimum viable product that we're starting with. As far as the Northstar, as I alluded to in the beginning, we have a ton of other products. We have a rich suite of products and Coinbase developer platform. We have user-custom wallets or what you might call an embedded wallet that works on Solana. You have custodial accounts, we have APIs for swaps, we have data APIs, we have primitives for payments and trading. And so I think all of these things are things that I think Solana builders aren't looking for, and things that in fact, we see Solana builders using on our platform today. And I think in the fullness of time would love for all of these things to be available conveniently wrapped in SDP so that Solana developers get them out of the box. That's fantastic. Yeah, and we certainly look forward to getting a lot of the other extra features embedded soon enough. I guess my next question is more just focused about Solana. And, of course, coming from a Coinbase perspective, you guys are multi-chain, of course, you build up base. Now I guess I'm curious from your product building experience of CBP. And what does that look like, especially just... Even from a developer perspective of building things on Solana? And what do you think are the highlights that you would like to talk about, um, looking at Solana and what it means for financial institutions? Yeah, so you're right. We're, we're multi chain. We want to support builders wherever it is they choose to build, whatever chain that is. So our wallets support all EVM chains as well as Solana. We see builders building on both at massive scale. I think considerations for an enterprise institution, these kind of FinTechs payment service providers, banks and brokerages, it's really, I think, intuitive that they're looking for scale, security, a simple developer experience, and cost efficiency really matters a lot. That's what they look for in a blockchain. In some cases, the blockchain is like a technical implementation that's not going to be exposed to their users, and they're going to pick one, and it's a technical choice of provider, essentially. And so, they'reising on those different dimensions. And I think Solana, the way that it's built is really powerful. It's among the top in terms of the sort of cost efficiency benefits that you get, the scale benefits that you get. The way that the accounts are sort of structured to take advantage of kind of modern multi core compute structures. There's a lot of advantages there that I think institutions see. The other is that there are sometimes enterprises that might want to enable multiple blockchains, especially if it's like a trading use case. And so, what one consideration there is not just the technical underpinnings of the blockchain, where I think Celana is very strong, but also what is the critical mass of users and personas that you see? So they might look at Celana and see, well, there's a ton of AI agents activity, and we want to plug into this emerging agent economy. We see a lot of compelling activity there. They might choose Solana for that reason. Or they might see that they're trying to enable trading use cases and in on-chain trading in particular, and they see a lot of a nexus and critical mass of that kind of activity on Solana. So I think there are various maybe cohorts or personas of users that have gravitated to Solana for a variety of reasons in the things that they're optimizing for on the user side. And so, if you have enterprises that want to go after those kind of cohorts of users, that can be another reason beyond just the technical underpinnings of the blockchain that they might gravitate towards Solana as well. Great. And I guess my last question for you is sort sort of like thinking in the next six to nine months, right? Some of the more ready to go type of product features we can start already collaborating together, as well as more ambitious ones. I guess maybe just starting on the ramp experience, because I think that this is quite a critical one. Just thinking about how to enable that seamless money movement between fiat and stablecoins. And, you know, therefore, what does SDP can provide inside SDP? about how to enable a seamless money movement between fiat and stable coins and what SDP can provide inside SDP. And then the other more futuristic, as I'm thinking out loud is there are a lot of people talking about on-chain FX within the trading context and stuff like that. I'm just curious about how you guys are thinking about that angle as well. Yeah, I think there's a lot more we can do. Like I said, we have a rich fleet of products We're eager to integrate into this lot of developer platform. You mentioned ramps specifically, so that's one that I think is just an obvious one. We see a lot of Solana builders using our on ramps and off ramps today. We have on ramp and off ramp APIs for programmatic or we might call headless, where you can kind of white label what the experience looks like for the end user of converting between fiat and crypto and back. And then we also have all the widgets or a component that we provide for onramping, where if you want something that's more like a Coinbase branded, some folks really want to avoid that. And some folks really want that. It makes users feel more secure and more trust in their app. We have a widget that's more on the onramp side, as well. So those are definitely things we want to integrate today. There's a lot of investment that we're making in those products in terms of expanding the breadth of payment method supported, the breadth of geographies in which users can do these things, and just making that really seamless. So, a lot more that I want to do there, and it's obviously something that's important to builders. Right? If you're building something in crypto, you need users to be able to onboard or on-r ramp their Fiat funds to get crypto so that they can do things with that crypto in your app, payments, trading, cross-border remittance, whatever it might be. You mentioned, I think, Apex. So I think there's just a lot of like payment use cases kind of within enterprises where they might have multiple legal entities around the world. They need to move money back and forth. They need to hedge risk around cruelty, exposure to things like that. I think we want to make it simpler. I know Solana wants to make it simpler for folks building on Solana for these use cases. So a lot more that we can do there. And then for end users that might be earning money in one currency in one country, want to send money to relatives of clients in another currency in another country, and do that in a really fast and really cost-efficient way using on-chain Rails. and Solana is great for those use cases. And then, of course, there's a bunch of feature development that we're engaging in where there are features we have today that work on same chains, not others. And I want to support Solana everywhere we can. So think one example is our on-chain swap. So we have an API for our chain swaps, and we want to add Solana there. Another example is our data APIs, where we have this SQL API where you can just write a SQL query and get on-chain data without needing an indexer, and I know that's a pain point for some builders on Solana. We want to add support there to help with that pain. So lots of things that we want to build that I think will be relevant to Solana builders, and we want to expose through STP so that it's all wrapped in one nice package with other infra providers and just dead simple for builders. Yeah those are all the things exactly what we want, and it's really exciting because you really touch on a lot of the things I wanted to get to because as you know, for v2 we want to push out the training module. And I think, given this is the bread and butter of you guys, I think there's a lot of things that we can collaborate together. So, great having you here Josh, today with me. So, thank you so much for you time, I'm looking forward to working with you. Likewise, thanks Catherine.
